desc_wei: Northern dynasty established by Cao Cao, controlling the Emperor.
desc_shu: Shu kingdom established by Liu Bei, centered in Sichuan.
desc_wu: Eastern Wu kingdom established by Sun Quan, controlling Jiangdong.
desc_zhou_west: Western Zhou capital at Haojing, modern Xi'an.
desc_zhou_east: Eastern Zhou capital at Luoyang, Henan.
desc_spring_autumn: Spring and Autumn period of feudal states contending.
desc_warring_states: Warring States period of seven powerful states.
desc_qi: Qi State during Spring and Autumn, centered in Shandong.
desc_chu: Chu State during Spring and Autumn, centered in Hubei.
desc_liang: Southern Liang dynasty of Southern and Northern Dynasties.
desc_sui_dadu: Sui Dynasty Daxing City, later Tang Chang'an.
desc_tang_changan: Tang capital Chang'an, Silk Road origin.
desc_tang_luoyang: Tang eastern capital Luoyang, Wu Zetian's capital.
desc_min: Min Kingdom during Five Dynasties, Fujian.
desc_wu_wu: Wu Kingdom during Five Dynasties, Jiangsu.
desc_song_north: Northern Song capital Kaifeng, northern China.
desc_song_south: Southern Song capital Lin'an (Hangzhou), southern China.
desc_ming_beijing: Ming capital after moving to Beijing.
desc_shang: First historically confirmed dynasty, known for bronze casting and oracle bone script.
desc_zhou: Longest-lasting dynasty, established the Mandate of Heaven and saw the rise of Confucianism.
desc_qin: First unified empire, standardized writing, currency, and built the initial Great Wall.
desc_han: Golden age of Chinese civilization, opened the Silk Road and invented paper.
desc_tang: Cosmopolitan golden age, peak of Chinese poetry and Buddhist influence.
desc_sui: Brief but pivotal reunification, rebuilt Grand Canal and unified China before Tang.
desc_three_kingdoms: Period of division between Wei, Shu, Wu after Han collapse.
desc_jin: Jin Dynasty reunified south after Three Kingdoms, later divided into Eastern and Western Jin.
desc_southern_northern: Southern dynasties (420-589) coexisted with Northern dynasties (439-581) in China.
desc_song: Economic and technological revolution, invented gunpowder, compass, and movable type printing.
desc_yuan: Mongol-ruled dynasty, part of the vast Mongol Empire, facilitated East-West exchange.
desc_ming: Native Chinese restoration, built the Forbidden City and sent Zheng He's treasure fleets.
desc_qing: Last imperial dynasty, expanded borders to modern China's extent.
desc_battle_muye: Decisive battle where Zhou overthrew the Shang dynasty.
desc_battle_julu: Decisive battle leading to the fall of the Qin dynasty.
desc_battle_chibi: Famous naval battle that established the Three Kingdoms period.
desc_capital_xian: Ancient capital for multiple dynasties, eastern terminus of the Silk Road.
desc_capital_beijing: Capital during Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties, home to the Forbidden City.
desc_great_wall: Series of walls and fortifications to protect against northern invasions.
desc_grand_canal: Longest artificial river in the world, connected northern and southern China.
